headline: Completing the five pre-declared variants 001 had cut: the paper's "in-work transfer beats demogrant" ranking is robust — Ψ_w < Ψ_d holds for 8 of 10 stable countries in 2026 and 75–100% of them under every variant (dispersion, hours, children, rent, SSC basis); bottom-quintile PTR fell a median −3.2 pp over 2009→2026.

notes: This is the continuation of followup/001-living-update: 001's headline (14 countries x 2009-2026) and all six gates were reused and reproduced bit-for-bit; this session completed the five secondary variants 001 had cut without budget justification.
Headline regime is V4 (q=0): 7 of 14 countries triggered no meaningful unemployment benefit in the hypothetical households (pre-declared rule 3).

Ψ levels are unstable for the lower deciles because bottom-decile PTR/MTR approach 100% (participation traps); Ψ counts are over the 'stable' countries only, and this instability is itself a finding. Robust deliverables are the decile profiles and the bottom-quintile PTR change.
Fixed an inherited bug: V5 rent was never applied (xhcrt hard-coded to 0); corrected and re-run.

Out of scope (stated as limits): UK (left EUROMOD), representative-microdata claims, policy years 2005-2008, elasticity re-estimation (Study B). Bottom-decile rates have no external TaxBEN benchmark; they rest on internal probes (IE hours PASS, DE Midijob inconclusive).
